terms.gloss: bury the hatchet, lay aside a grudge
evidence: Suet. Caes. 73: occāsiōne oblātā simultātēs dēpōnere (Lewis & Short s.v. occāsiō)
terms.comment: Simultās is a grudge or feud between two people (Lewis & Short: dissension, rivalry, animosity); dēpōnere, to lay down.

sources: Lewis & Short: simultas · Lewis & Short: depono
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 94, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
